messages:
maria: Heads-up — FinOps flagged a weird spike in GPU spend mapped to `team:unknown`. Looks like a chain of stale labels from nodepools created by autoscaler last month.

maria: Quick dump from cost export: `account=redwood-prod, resource=ec2, tag:team=, tag:service=inference` — huge tail of small runs.

dave: ugh. Is this the same thing where nodepool names changed and the kube labels didn’t get propagated? :thinking_face:

simon: Probable. We saw autoscaler recreate nodes when rolling the instance type. The new nodes came up with cloud tags but kubelets never picked up the pod-level labels because bootstrap script crashed once.

arjun: Do we have an audit trail? billingbot, can you paste the last 7d tag-unassigned report?

billingbot: Report: 2026-03-10..2026-03-17 — 423 untagged GPU instances, est $18,600. Top regions: us-west-2 (58%), eu-west-1 (31%). Top orphan source: autoscaler-nodepool-3.

maria: thanks. I can repro a small sample. Here's the aws cli we used to find node tags:
```bash
aws --profile prod ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=*autoscaler-nodepool-3*" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,Tags]' --output text
```
output: a bunch of instances with empty `team` tag or `team:unknown`.

dave: From chargeback side, those ended up in the unallocated bucket and got spread evenly — meaning teams with reservations didn't benefit. Need to decide: backfill tags and re-run allocation or absorb one-time adjustment?

simon: Short-term fix: backfill kube/node labels for currently running nodes and add a cron to reapply tags for new nodes until bootstrap is fixed. Longer: fix bootstrap script and add e2e that ensures tags sync on join.

arjun: Who can run the backfill script and coordinate with FinOps to reclassify costs? We should also identify any reserved capacity (savings plan / RI) that got applied incorrectly.

maria: I can run the backfill in us-west-2 today (low traffic window). Script is simple: fetch nodes missing `team` label, map to nodepool metadata in aws tags, patch via `kubectl label node`.

maria: Sample one-liner:
```bash
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | grep autoscaler-nodepool-3); do t=$(aws ec2 describe-tags --filters "Name=resource-id,Values=$(echo $n | cut -d/ -f2)" "Name=tag:team" --query 'Tags[0].Value' --output text); kubectl label node $(echo $n | cut -d/ -f2) team=$t --overwrite; done
```

dave: Please also dump the invoice IDs and timestamps for those instances before and after backfill so FinOps can re-run allocation. I’ll open a billing recalculation ticket with accounting.

billingbot: Filed ticket ACCT-1294: request reallocation for untagged GPU spend 2026-03-01..2026-03-17. Attachments requested: node list, instance IDs, evidence of tag backfill.

arjun: Note on reserved capacity: If those instances were part of reserved pool (dedicated vs on-demand mix), we need to ensure commitments applied to proper cost centers. Simon — can you check which nodepool consumed Reserved Instances / Savings Plans?

simon: On it. Early result: autoscaler-nodepool-3 was a mixed pool using spare dedicated capacity under the infra commitment; about 42% of hours charged to infra-commitment, 58% billed as on-demand — messy. If we reassign tags, commit benefits might shift across teams.

maria: Suggestion: re-run allocation once tags are backfilled but mark any shift greater than $1k as a 'manual review' before applying chargebacks to product teams. We should avoid surprising teams with retro charges.

dave: Agreed. FinOps preference: create an adjustment window (30d) and include notes in invoices. If net adjustment < $5k we absorb to infra overhead. >$5k requires approval from GTM lead.

arjun: Ok timeline:
- Today: maria runs backfill in us-west-2 (ETA 2h)
- Tomorrow: simon finishes reserved vs on-demand mapping (ETA EOD)
- Billing: dave prepares recalculation package once we have node/instance evidence (ETA +48h)

maria: Running now, posting status. :rocket:

maria: Done with backfill in us-west-2 — patched 112 nodes, labels now reflect `team` and `product`.

maria: I pushed the node list to the ACCT-1294 ticket and included the `kubectl get nodes -L team,product` output.

billingbot: ACCT-1294 updated: evidence received. Automated allocation queued (run at 03:00 UTC).

dave: Once automated allocation completes, I'll compare to original export and flag any >$1k movements. If none, we'll apply changes and update internal chargeback dashboards. If there are big shifts, I'll loop in CS and GTM.

simon: Reserve mapping complete. Summary: autoscaler-nodepool-3 consumed ~720 GPU-hours under infra commitment and ~980 GPU-hours on-demand in the window. If we reattribute, infra commit usage drops ~18% and product teams pick it up.

arjun: For prevention: add a k8s admission check to fail node join without required labels, add robust bootstrap retry, and add a tag-sync controller. Also add a daily alert when >5% of GPU pool has `team` unset.

maria: Filing infra ticket INFRA-2125 with the fixes above. Will add a short postmortem and a runbook for similar future incidents.

dave: Thanks all. Good catch. :thumbsup:

simon: One note — eu-west-1 still has ~30 untagged nodes. I'll run backfill there after apac maintenance window tomorrow.

maria: ack — keep me posted.

arjun: Closing loop: once billing calc is in and FinOps confirms, we'll decide absorb vs backcharge. Leave thread open until resolved.

billingbot: Allocation job finished: reallocation shows $16,900 reattributed from unallocated -> teams. Pending dave review.

dave: Reviewing now. Will post final decision by EOD.

maria: thanks everyone.
